Import/export are in, inside **⚙ Settings**. Reload **http://maker:4001/app.html**, then:

**Block F — import/export standard bookmarks HTML.**
> 1. Open **⚙ Settings** → **Export bookmarks.html**. Your browser downloads a `bookmarks.html` in the standard Netscape format that Chrome, Firefox and Safari all understand — each entry carries its **title, tags (`TAGS="…"`), and original date (`ADD_DATE`)**.
> 2. (Optional) Open that downloaded file in a text editor to see the standard structure, or import it straight into a real browser to confirm it's compatible.
> 3. Back in **⚙ Settings** → **Import bookmarks.html…**, choose that same file (or a real export from your browser). It adds the bookmarks, **keeping their titles, tags and dates**, and **skips any links you already have** — you'll see a summary like *"Imported N, skipped M already-saved."*

A few things to confirm:

- Export/import using the **standard browser bookmarks file** (so it round-trips with real browsers) — is that the right interchange format, or did you have a specific app's format in mind?
- On import, I **skip links you already have** (by the same near-duplicate rule) rather than duplicating them. Agree that's the right default?
- Standard bookmark files carry title/tags/dates but have **no place for your private notes, read-later/archive state, or saved copies** — so those don't travel in this format. Is exporting the **standard fields only** acceptable, or would you also want a separate **full backup** (everything, including notes and states) as its own option?
